title: GM gives its most important trucks a new UI—and includes CarPlay
gist: For model-year 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra pickups, General Motors ships a minimalist new instrument-cluster and infotainment UI that keeps Apple CarPlay and Android Auto phone casting — the opposite of the decision GM made for its EVs — while restoring physical HVAC controls and adding a polarized front-passenger screen with HDMI input and a full web browser. GM's own press release describes the system as a single scalable foundation across electric, gas and diesel vehicles, hinting the EV CarPlay ban may not survive.

themes.theme: CarPlay reversal signal in GM's highest-margin product

insights.claim: General Motors is keeping Apple CarPlay and Android Auto phone casting in the model-year 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra, despite having stripped that capability from its newer electric vehicles.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: GM is protecting its profit-center trucks from the consumer backlash it absorbed on EVs, which caps the software-services revenue thesis built on owning the screen.
insights.quote: unlike GM’s electric vehicles, these trucks still let you cast your Apple or Android phone to the infotainment system
insights.locator: General Motors is about to launch new versions of its best-selling

insights.claim: GM's press release describes the new infotainment system as "a single scalable foundation across electric, gas and diesel-powered vehicles," language that implies the same CarPlay-supporting platform could reach EVs.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: If the platform is truly shared, GM's EV phone-casting ban becomes a policy toggle rather than an architecture constraint — a reversal investors should treat as live.
insights.quote: as a single scalable foundation across electric, gas and diesel-powered vehicles, it transforms time spent behind the wheel into an effortless, personalized journey
insights.locator: GM’s spokesperson wouldn’t be drawn on whether this means

insights.claim: GM's spokesperson declined to say whether keeping phone casting in trucks signals a corporate retreat from the company's prior anti-CarPlay stance on EVs.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A non-denial on a walked-back strategy is the tell to watch ahead of any formal EV software policy change.
insights.locator: GM’s spokesperson wouldn’t be drawn on whether this means

insights.claim: GM had justified removing phone casting from EVs by claiming it would deliver a better, more unified customer experience, a rationale undercut by shipping casting in its newest and most important trucks.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: The stated rationale for locking out Apple and Google looks like a revenue play, not a UX play; expect similar walk-backs at other OEMs that followed GM.
insights.locator: GM made the decision to drop Apple CarPlay and Android Auto phone casting

insights.claim: Rather than isolating phone casting, GM now embeds CarPlay and Android Auto in a large tile occupying most of the infotainment screen with a side card for native apps such as towing or music, so projection and native software coexist.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: The coexistence layout is the compromise model: OEMs keep vehicle-specific data surfaces monetizable while conceding the media and nav layer to phones.
insights.locator: And it has done a better job of integrating CarPlay and Android Auto

insights.claim: Porsche took a similar approach of working with rather than against customers who want CarPlay, establishing a precedent that premium OEMs can integrate phone projection without ceding their own interface.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Two large OEMs converging on coexistence suggests the industry-wide 'kick out Apple' thesis is losing, favoring Apple's automotive position.
insights.locator: Porsche took a similar approach to working with, rather than against

themes.theme: Android Automotive underneath, redesigned on top

insights.claim: The central infotainment screen in the new trucks still runs on Android Automotive OS, so GM's UI overhaul is a software layer change rather than a platform change.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Google retains the underlying automotive OS position in GM's highest-volume vehicles regardless of the CarPlay question.
insights.quote: The central infotainment screen still runs on Android Automotive OS

insights.claim: GM's new home screen shows a split view with a full map rather than the previously limited split-screen map, letting users search or report road conditions without being thrown out of the home screen.
insights.speaker: Colin McCormick, group product manager at GM
insights.so_what: Removing navigation friction is how OEMs try to keep drivers inside native software instead of reaching for the phone.
insights.quote: Here, you can do everything that full screen maps can do right inside this window

insights.claim: GM added Android-style notifications and user-creatable quick actions to the infotainment system, and fixed app behavior so accepting a phone call no longer dumps the user out of the active app into the dialer.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: These are basic smartphone-parity fixes shipping in 2027 model years — evidence of how far behind OEM software still is.
insights.locator: GM has also integrated more Android-like notifications

themes.theme: Minimalist cluster design and physical controls returning

insights.claim: GM's new instrument cluster uses a permanently black background with local dimming technology and deliberately reduced visual noise, a reversal of the maximalist screen designs the automaker previously shipped.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Local-dimming black-background clusters favor OLED/mini-LED display suppliers over conventional automotive LCD panels.
insights.locator: Although GM showed us video of the main instrument cluster

insights.claim: The truck cluster offers four purpose-built views — standard dials, a driver-assist view that turns green when Super Cruise is active and renders fused sensor output, an off-road view with angles and differential settings, and a towing view.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Purpose-built off-road and towing modes are how GM justifies premium trim pricing and differentiates from phone-projected interfaces it cannot control.
insights.locator: There are a number of different views

insights.claim: GM includes an extreme minimalist cluster mode showing only large white speed digits, echoing the night mode Saab once offered, and keeps a permanent bottom strip with fuel level, drive mode and warning lights across all views.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Reviving a decades-old ergonomics idea signals that 'less screen' is becoming a marketable feature rather than a cost cut.
insights.locator: But there’s also an even more minimalist version

insights.claim: The new trucks retain physical dials for temperature and physical buttons for fan speed and demisting, alongside a dedicated on-screen climate row.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Physical HVAC controls returning in a flagship 2027 vehicle marks the end of the all-touchscreen interior trend and supports automotive switch/haptics suppliers.
insights.quote: Note the real controls for the HVAC.
insights.locator: A dedicated row at the bottom of the screen is for the climate controls

insights.claim: After a demo of the new system, the reviewer concluded GM has been listening to constructive feedback to improve its products, framing this release as a correction of prior interface decisions.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Critic sentiment turning positive on GM software reduces a reputational drag that had been cited against its EV and subscription strategy.
insights.locator: The automaker has gone for a more minimalist approach

themes.theme: The passenger screen becomes standard equipment

insights.claim: A dedicated front-passenger infotainment screen will be available on the Silverado and Sierra, coated with a polarized filter so the driver cannot see the content.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Passenger displays spreading from luxury brands into mass-market pickups expands the addressable market for automotive display and polarizing-film suppliers.
insights.locator: Passenger screens are here to stay

insights.claim: The passenger screen accepts video over HDMI from a port at the passenger's knee, pairs with Bluetooth headphones so audio need not go through the truck speakers, runs native streaming apps, and includes a full web browser with the smartphone usable as a keyboard.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A browser-capable second screen turns the vehicle into another streaming endpoint, opening in-car content and advertising inventory for media companies.
insights.locator: This can be streaming content or video piped in via HDMI

insights.claim: The reviewer concedes that criticism of OEMs adding passenger dash screens is now a losing battle, treating the feature as an irreversible industry trend.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Assume screen count per vehicle keeps rising; size display-supplier content-per-vehicle estimates accordingly.
insights.quote: Complaining about the trend of OEMs putting an extra infotainment screen in the dash for the front passenger is evidently a losing battle now
insights.locator: Passenger screens are here to stay
